Desktop Publishing · Week 1 · Title

What desktop publishing is — and the tools for it

Desktop publishing is designing pages to be read — on paper or on screen. Free tools do it well.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Desktop Publishing · Week 1 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Say what desktop publishing is, with five examples
  • Tell print design from screen design
  • Choose a free tool for a job
Desktop Publishing · Week 1 · Idea 1

Understand it

Desktop publishing (DTP) is arranging text and pictures on a page so people can read and use it: flyers, posters, newsletters, certificates, brochures, programmes, menus.

Good design is not decoration. A flyer must be read in three seconds from across the road; a programme must be found in the dark; a certificate must look official.

The tools (all free):

  • Canva — browser and phone, templates, easy sharing.
  • Google Docs / Slides — quick documents and single pages.
  • LibreOffice Draw/Writer — offline, on any computer.
  • Scribus — professional page layout for print, free.

Desktop Publishing · Week 1 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Collect five printed things (a flyer, a programme, a receipt, a certificate, a menu)
  2. Say who each is for and what it must do
  3. Open Canva and one other free tool

Need a hand? For each printed thing, answer: who is it for? what must they do after reading it?

Done early? Find one design that works badly and say exactly what you would change.

Desktop Publishing · Week 1 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • A shop wants 500 flyers printed and also a post for WhatsApp. What is the main difference to plan for?
  • Show your five collected printed things and explain, for one of them, who it is for and what it must make them do.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.

Desktop Publishing · Week 1 · Home

At home this week

Read and explore

  • GCFGlobal — Beginning Graphic Design — Free, short, illustrated lessons on layout, type and colour; no account needed.
  • Scribus — Free, professional desktop publishing for Windows, Mac and Linux — what the print trade uses for free.
  • LibreOffice Help — Free office suite; Draw and Writer can lay out a flyer or newsletter.
